markets.question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. eventMetadata.context_description: The 2028 presidential nomination contests remain wide open more than two years before the primaries, as shown by the dispersed trader probabilities across over 40 candidates with no single contender exceeding 22%. On the Republican side, current administration figures such as JD Vance hold the lead due to visibility from the prior cycle, while senators and governors like Marco Rubio and Ron DeSantis compete for support among party voters. Democratic probabilities spread among governors including Gavin Newsom and Josh Shapiro plus senators and House members reflect similar early positioning without consolidated polling or endorsements. The tight field stems from the lack of an incumbent, fluid primary dynamics, and uncertainty over voter coalitions in key states, with potential separation likely from 2026 midterm results, confirmation votes, or early campaign announcements that shift perceived paths to the nomination.
